 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Anil Kumar Sinha
 Oral Order

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2.
2.
The petitioner apprehends his arrest in connection with Alamganj Police Station Case No. 969 of 2023, registered for the offences under Sections 341/323/504/506/379/498(A) of the Indian Penal Code.
3. The prosecution story, as per the First Information Report, is that the marriage of the petitioner was solemnized with the opposite party no. 2 on 01.05.2023.

After the marriage, the petitioner started mentally as well as physically torturing the opposite party no. 2 for which she lodged a case at Mahila Thana, Purnia, bearing Mahila Police Station Case No. 40 of 2023, against the petitioner and his family members under Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.39938 of 2025(5) dt.27-11-2025 Section 341/323/342/498A/504/506/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

entities.text: Mahila Police Station Case No. 40 of 2023
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: It has further been alleged that on 10th October, 2023, the petitioner abused and threatened the informant on phone and on 11th October, 2023 when she was coming back from office towards her house at Bajrangapuri, the petitioner called her on phone and as the opposite party no. 2 reached near Sagar Sweets, she saw her husband standing with 2 to 3 persons.
Husband i.e. the petitioner stopped the opposite party no. 2 abused, slapped and threatened her and also snatched gold mangalsutra from the opposite party no. 2.

sentences.text: There is matrimonial discord between the husband and wife and several cases have been filed by the opposite party no. 2 against the petitioner.
The present case is the second matrimonial case filed by the opposite party no. 2 against the petitioner.

Apart from these cases, one Maintenance case,
bearing Maintenance Case No. 154 of 2025, has also been filed at Patna Sadar.

5. In order to explore amicable settlement of the dispute between the husband and wife on 15.10.2025, the petitioner as well as the opposite party no. 2 were asked to be physically present before this Court in order to explore the possibility of Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.39938 of 2025(5) dt.27-11-2025 settlement between them.

6. Subsequently, on 14.11.2025, the matter was adjourned for today i.e. 27.11.2025 and both the husband and wife, along with their parents and respective learned counsels, are present in-person before this Court in Chambers.

7. After prolonged discussion and deliberation both the parties have agreed for final settlement on terms and condition mentioned herebelow:-
i.

The petitioner is ready to pay a total sum of Rs. 35 Lakhs to the opposite party no.
2.

Out of the aforesaid amount, sum of Rs. 20 Lakhs shall be paid at the time of filing of divorce petition by mutual consent under Section 13(B) of the Hindu Marriage Act before 15th January, 2026, at Purnea.
ii. The remaining sum of Rs. 15 Lakhs shall be paid at the time of filing of affidavit before the Family Court at the time of second motion.

iii. Considering, the terms and condition arrived at between parties, in this proceeding, the Family Court may waive off the cooling period of six months and at the time of second motion a sum of Rs.
5 Lakh shall be paid and just before passing of Patna High Court CR.

MISC . No.39938 of 2025(5)
dt.27-11-2025 the final decree

, the balance amount of Rs. 10 Lakh shall be paid by the petitioner to the opposite party no. 2.
iv.

The Family Court, before signing the final decree of divorce on mutual consent, shall ensure that the entire sum of Rs. 35 Lakhs has been deposited by the petitioner in the bank account of the opposite party no. 2.
v.

The FIRs, lodged at Patna and Purnea, bearing Mahila Police Station Case No. 969 of 2023, dated 14.10.2023 and Mahila Police Station Case No. 40 of 2023, dated 04.10.2023 under Section 498A and other allied sections, shall not be pursued by the opposite party no. 2.

vi. The maintenance case, lodged at Patna having Maintenance Case No. 154 of 2025 filed by Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.39938 of 2025(5) dt.27-11-2025 opposite party no. 2, shall be withdrawn Tushar Bharti vs The State Of Bihar on 27 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15696614/
2 before final payment of Rs. 10 Lakh by the petitioner to the opposite party no. 2.
8.

9.
In view of the settlement arrived at between the parties, I am incline to grant anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

10. Let the petitioner, above named, in the event of his arrest/surrender before the learned Court below within a period of six weeks from today, be released on bail, upon furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (Ten Thousand) with two sureties of like amount, each, to the satisfaction of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate IV, Patna City, Patna, in connection with Alamganj Police Station Case No. 969 of 2023.
